body_markdown:
*−* *New analyses show a consistent efficacy signal with once-daily 60 mg remlifanserin across multiple measures of psychosis, with larger estimated treatment effects with increasing baseline psychosis severity*


SAN DIEGO—(BUSINESS WIRE)—


Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Nasdaq: ACAD) today presented additional data from the Phase 2 RADIANT trial evaluating remlifanserin for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Alzheimer’s disease psychosis (ADP) during an oral presentation at the 2026 Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) conference in Boston. Building on previously announced topline results, new analyses provided further evidence of a consistent efficacy signal with once-daily 60 mg remlifanserin across multiple measures of psychosis and new insights into treatment effect by baseline psychosis severity.


As previously reported, once-daily 60 mg remlifanserin narrowly missed the primary endpoint, with a −2.2-point improvement versus placebo on SAPS-H+D at Week 6 (p=0.0603), and achieved nominal significance on the key secondary endpoint, CGI-S-ADP (p=0.0077). The 30 mg dose showed minimal efficacy versus placebo, supporting a dose-response relationship.


New analyses presented at CTAD showed a consistent treatment effect with once-daily 60 mg remlifanserin across multiple measures of psychosis and timepoints:


- On the CGI-I-ADP, 60 mg was favored over placebo at Weeks 2, 4, and 6 (nominal p=0.0232, p=0.0082, and p=0.0208, respectively). At Week 6, 44.0% of patients receiving the 60 mg dose were improved or very much improved (CGI-I-ADP score of 1 or 2), compared with 31.8% receiving placebo.


- On the Neuropsychiatric Inventory/Neuropsychiatric Inventory Nursing Home (NPI/NPI-NH) psychosis score, 60 mg separated from placebo at Week 4 (nominal p=0.0084) and Week 6, where the LS mean change was −7.3 for the 60 mg dose versus −5.9 for placebo (nominal p=0.0385; effect size 0.29).


- On CGI-S-ADP, 60 mg separated from placebo at Week 4 (nominal p=0.0107) as well as Week 6.


Additionally, the estimated treatment effect on SAPS-H+D Total Score increased across progressively higher baseline psychosis severity thresholds.


“These new analyses strengthen the evidence of a consistent efficacy signal with once-daily 60 mg remlifanserin across multiple measures of psychosis and timepoints,” said Sanjeev Pathak, M.D., Senior Vice President, Head of Clinical Development. “The observed dose-response pattern, together with new insights into the relationship between baseline psychosis severity and estimated treatment effect, further reinforces our confidence in the activity of remlifanserin as we continue Phase 3 development.”


At the 60 mg dose, the observed safety and tolerability profiles of remlifanserin were consistent with previously reported topline findings. Rates of treatment-emergent adverse events (36.8% vs. 41.7%), drug-related adverse events (5.6% vs. 7.8%), serious adverse events (1.6% vs. 2.6%) and discontinuations due to adverse events (2.4% vs. 2.6%) were similar to or lower than those in the placebo group. There were no deaths in either remlifanserin arm. In the study, there was no negative impact on motor symptoms (Extrapyramidal Symptom Rating Scale – Abbreviated (ESRS-A)) or cognition (Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)) versus placebo, and no patient assessed had a QTcF above 480 msec or an increase of more than 60 msec.


Based on the Phase 2 findings, Acadia continues to advance the Phase 3 portion of the RADIANT clinical program, evaluating remlifanserin for ADP.


Additionally, remlifanserin is currently being investigated in an additional Phase 2 study to evaluate its efficacy, safety, and tolerability for the treatment of Lewy body dementia psychosis.


### About RADIANT


RADIANT is a global, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, operationally seamless Phase 2 and 3 clinical trial program evaluating remlifanserin for the treatment of hallucinations and delusions associated with Alzheimer’s disease psychosis (ADP). The Phase 2 portion of the program was designed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of remlifanserin at 60 mg and 30 mg once-daily doses compared with placebo. Patients who complete any of the RADIANT studies have the option of participating in a long-term open-label extension (OLE) study.


### About Alzheimer’s Disease Psychosis


According to the Alzheimer’s Association, more than 7 million people aged 65 years and older in the United States are living with Alzheimer’s disease (AD).1,2 Approximately 30% of patients with AD experience psychosis, commonly consisting of hallucinations and delusions.3,4 These symptoms may be frequent and may recur over time.5 A hallucination is defined as a perception-like experience that occurs without an external stimulus and is sensory (seen, heard, felt, tasted, sensed, smelled) in nature. A delusion is defined as a false, fixed belief despite evidence to the contrary.6 Psychosis in patients with dementia is associated with outcomes such as increased likelihood of nursing home placement, more severe dementia, and increased risk of morbidity and mortality.7,8 There is no FDA-approved drug for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease psychosis.


### About Remlifanserin


Remlifanserin is a novel, highly selective 5HT2A receptor inverse agonist being developed to treat Alzheimer’s disease psychosis and Lewy body dementia psychosis.
